title: Animal intelligence
examples: Do all intelligent animals use tools?
What is the most complex animal brain?
How do crows learn to use tools?

explain.say: Today we explore smart animals and how they use tools.

items: Crows are known for their clever problem-solving.
Octopuses have amazing intelligence and problem-solving skills.
Dolphins communicate using complex whistles and clicks.
Apes show advanced social behaviour and tool use.

explain.say: Crows are very smart birds that can remember human faces.
Octopuses are masters of disguise and problem-solving in the sea.
Dolphins use clicks and whistles to communicate with each other.
Apes are primates that live in groups and use tools in many ways.
Many animals use tools to help them find food or survive.

faq.q: Do all intelligent animals use tools?
faq.a: No, tool use is a complex behaviour seen in certain groups of animals. It requires advanced planning and understanding of physics.
asks: Is tool use only for humans?

faq.q: How do we know an animal is intelligent?
faq.a: Scientists look at things like problem-solving ability, communication complexity, and memory retention. These are key signs of high intelligence.
asks: What is a sign of smart animals?

faq.q: What is camouflage, and which animal uses it well?
faq.a: Camouflage is the ability to blend into the surroundings to avoid being seen. Octopuses are famous for changing their skin colour quickly.
asks: What is blending into the background?

faq.q: What is the difference between a tool and natural behaviour?
faq.a: A tool is an object that an animal modifies or uses to achieve a goal. Natural behaviour is instinctual action without modifying an object.
asks: Is a rock always a tool?
What counts as using a tool?

faq.a: Dolphins use a variety of sounds, including whistles and clicks, which help them navigate and talk to others.

facts: Crows can recognize human faces and remember them for years.
Octopuses have a high level of intelligence allowing them to solve puzzles.
Dolphins use echolocation, sending out sounds to map their environment.
Apes use tools in ways that are specific to their environment.

quiz.say: Which animal is known for its ability to change its skin colour?
quiz.why: Octopuses are famous for their remarkable ability to change their skin colour for camouflage.

wrong.1: Crows are smart, but they are not primarily known for changing their skin colour.
wrong.2: Dolphins use sound for communication, not skin colour changes.
wrong.3: Apes are known for tool use, but camouflage is the octopus's specialty.

quiz.say: If an animal uses a stick to catch fish, what is the stick acting as?
quiz.why: The stick is being used by the animal to help it achieve a goal, making it a tool.

wrong.0: While it is natural, calling it only that ignores its function as a tool.
wrong.2: This ignores the action; the object only becomes a tool when used purposefully.
wrong.3: A stick is not food, even if the animal eats it later.

quiz.say: Which group of animals is known for complex social structures and tool use?
quiz.why: Apes are primates known for complex social living and advanced tool use in their environment.

wrong.0: Octopuses are intelligent, but apes are highlighted for their primate social complexity.
wrong.1: Dolphins are highly intelligent, but apes fit the description of complex social primate groups.
wrong.3: Crows are very smart, but apes are specifically noted for complex social structures.
